name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,266

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old man in need of drink and a sunshade

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man
to lap is to drink as a cat does
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thirsty old fellow on a hot day wants a drink and somewhere shady to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A palapa is a Mexican open-sided shelter thatched with palm leaves, used on beaches for shade from the sun.

clue.text: Mammals turning up in plain and peak

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: stark means plain or bare
a cap is a peak or summit, as in an ice cap on a mountain

explanation.surface: Some animals appear on open plains and mountain tops.
explanation.walkthrough: STARK and CAP together, read upwards, give PACK RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack rats are North American wood rats, rodents known for hoarding objects in their nests.

clue.text: Youth, within two years RAF officer, one spotted with wings

indicators.note: within says the officer sits inside the pair of years

blocks.note: a lad is a youth
Y is the abbreviation for year, taken twice
FL abbreviates Flight Lieutenant, a Royal Air Force rank

explanation.surface: A young man, after two years in the air force, becomes an officer with his wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' looks like the RAF pilot's badge; it describes the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladyfly is an old name for the ladybird, a small spotted beetle that flies with wings under its hard wing cases.

clue.text: “Finnish” female athlete initially enters for run, after quiet attempt to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it held inside, so the attempt wraps around energy
initially points to only the opening letter of the athlete
enters for says one letter comes in to take the place of another, the run letter

blocks.note: p (piano) means quiet in music
a try is an attempt
E is the symbol for energy in physics
a girl is a female
the opening letter of athlete
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A female athlete hoping to make the finish of a race saves her energy after a quiet start.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes on “Finnish” flag a pun: not the nationality but fin-ish, to do with fins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterygial means relating to fins or wings, so it can be playfully described as fin-ish, having to do with fins.

clue.text: New Year do’s talked of for caretaker

indicators.note: talked of says we hear the word rather than read it

blocks.note: the first day of the year, Jan 1, written JAN I
a do is a swindle or trick, so do's suggests tricks

explanation.surface: Someone describes the New Year's Eve parties to the building caretaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do's' looks like parties; here a do is a con or trick. JAN I is the first of January.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitrix is a female janitor, a person employed to look after and clean a building.

clue.text: Henry in Accounts has World Nations Anthem released? It’s not everyone’s thing

indicators.note: in places Henry between the two account abbreviations

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account; accounts plural gives two of them
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
UN is the United Nations
an anthem is a song
something released is out

explanation.surface: A man called Henry in the finance department has put out a world anthem, which not everyone will like.
explanation.walkthrough: AC H AC makes the A CHAC that opens the French phrase A CHACUN SON GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The French saying means each to his own taste, conceding that something may please some people but not all.

clue.text: False ideas of a philosopher — and artificial language, note

blocks.note: Ido is a constructed language derived from Esperanto
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A philosopher's mistaken notions are paired with a made-up language and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Idola is Francis Bacon's term for the fallacies, or idols, that mislead human understanding.

clue.text: Master at home with pupil once restriction lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised from bottom to top, so read upwards

blocks.note: someone at home is in
an OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
a bar is a restriction or ban

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster at home with a former student once a ban has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, OB and BAR are joined then turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabboni is a Hebrew title of respect meaning my teacher, used for Jesus in the Gospel of John.

clue.text: Hospital DJ looking up American or Greek ancestor

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
a DJ, dinner jacket, is a tux
US abbreviates American

explanation.surface: A hospital radio disc jockey searches for American or Greek ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DJ' looks like a disc jockey; it is a dinner jacket. Only the first two pieces are turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Xuthus in Greek myth was a son of Hellen and father of Ion and Achaeus, forefather of Ionians and Achaeans.

clue.text: Character of Lear, tho deaf OK, wasn’t mad

indicators.note: mad means crazy and disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of these four words, all used

explanation.surface: King Lear, though deaf, was not mad, someone insists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's King Lear, who goes mad; it is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akond of Swat is the subject of a nonsense poem by Edward Lear, so he is a figure from Lear's verse.

clue.text: Welcome notice mostly to avoid backing poet’s right to entertainment

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
backing means moving backwards, so the whole string is read from the end

blocks.note: hi is a word of welcome
to heed is to notice or pay attention
to duck is to avoid

explanation.surface: A notice of welcome tries to dodge supporting a poet's claim to be entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: HI, HEED and DUC are joined, then the lot is reversed. 'Poet's' signals a word used by Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser, cuddeehih is the Irish lord's right to food and hospitality from a tenant, an entitlement to be entertained.

clue.text: What can spoil hide, swapping parts of anti-wrinkle treatment

indicators.note: swapping parts says the front and back sections of the word change places

blocks.note: Botox is a cosmetic injection used to smooth wrinkles

explanation.surface: A cosmetic treatment against wrinkles might ruin your skin.
explanation.walkthrough: BOT and OX swap places. 'Hide' looks like a verb; it is an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-bot is the larva of a warble fly, which burrows under cattle skin and leaves holes that damage leather.

clue.text: Proud fairy had an oddly invisible Asian rhino!

definitions.note: rhino is slang for money; the answer is a currency

indicators.note: oddly invisible says the odd-numbered letters vanish, leaving only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: A proud fairy owned a rare Asian rhinoceros that nobody could see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' looks like the animal; in British slang rhino means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rufiyaa is the currency of the Maldives, so it is a sum of Asian money.

clue.text: Tea ceremony to get to, one November out in China briefly

indicators.note: out says one of the November letters is removed
in places the shortened word inside the other
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a mate is a chum
to get to someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: Someone heads out to a tea ceremony in China, minus one November date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in rhyming slang china plate means mate. 'Get to' means irritate, not arrive at.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanoyu is the Japanese ritual of preparing and serving powdered green tea.

clue.text: Sweetbreads unhealthy directly alongside mincemeat sandwiches

indicators.note: directly alongside says the two words are butted together with nothing between them
sandwiches says only what is held in the middle of the joined words is kept, the outer bread discarded

blocks.note: taken as written; only its tail is kept
taken as written; only its head is kept

explanation.surface: Sweetbreads served with mincemeat make a rich and unhealthy sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directly alongside' tells you to butt the two words together; the letters run across where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbreads are the thymus glands of calves or lambs eaten as offal, and thymi is the plural of thymus.

clue.text: Fresh opening for thrush in choir of birds

indicators.note: an opening is a start, so only the first letter of the bird is used
fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the opening letter of thrush
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrush makes a fresh start among a choir of songbirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the thrush in the choir; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithic is an adjective meaning relating to or characteristic of birds, from the Greek for bird.

clue.text: I’m with different broadcaster for gig

indicators.note: different says the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A musician says they've switched to a new broadcaster for a concert booking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gig' looks like a concert; it is a light carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tim-whisky was a light open one-horse carriage of the eighteenth century, a type of gig.

clue.text: Old minister’s wife with gentle touch after sex?

indicators.note: after says the touch follows the number in the order of letters

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals
a caress is a gentle touch

explanation.surface: A clergyman's wife is described tenderly after lovemaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' looks like intercourse; it is the Latin numeral six.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicaress was the wife of a vicar, a parish clergyman, an archaic term for a minister's spouse.

clue.text: No good leaving, avoiding going in for early piece

indicators.note: leaving says the letters for no good depart from the word
going in places the shortened word inside the other

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
eluding means avoiding
NG is a common abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A worthless person departs, dodging having to go in early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link before the definition; it is a piece of the wordplay, and 'early piece' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A preludio is a prelude, an introductory musical movement that comes before the main work.

clue.text: Author of dossier’s final ambition spelled out first for lecturer

indicators.note: final points to only the closing letter of the dossier

blocks.note: the closing letter of dossier
an end is an aim or ambition
the first letter of lecturer is L, and spelled out as a name it is ell

explanation.surface: A writer's goal for a dossier is explained first to a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelled out' means write the letter as its name: L becomes ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Rendell was a British crime novelist, creator of Inspector Wexford.

clue.text: Middle East pair coming between leaders of Hong Kong and India’s emperor

blocks.note: ME abbreviates Middle East

blocks.clueFragment: pair coming between leaders of Hong Kong
blocks.note: in the alphabet the two letters between the first letters of Hong and Kong are I and J
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two Middle Eastern figures mediate between the heads of Hong Kong and India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of Hong Kong' gives H and K, and the pair of letters between them in the alphabet is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Meiji was the Japanese emperor who reigned from 1867 to 1912, presiding over Japan's modernisation.

clue.text: Local court’s abbreviated description of Broadway?

blocks.note: Broadway is in New York, a road

explanation.surface: A pub's courtyard is given a short write-up as Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub, an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn-yard is the courtyard of an inn; local is pub slang and a court is an enclosed yard.

clue.text: Content regulators with joint statement primarily supporting board deputy

indicators.note: primarily points to only the first letter of statement
in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so these pieces come after

blocks.note: VC abbreviates vice-chairman, the deputy of a board
the hip is a joint
the first letter of statement

explanation.surface: Regulators issue a joint statement backing the deputy chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy; it is TV content.
explanation.definitionFit: V-chips are devices in television sets that let parents block programmes rated violent or unsuitable.

clue.text: Officiating at game is beyond one hundred

blocks.note: if something is beyond you, you can't do it
to ref is to referee, officiating at a game

explanation.surface: Refereeing a match is more than one hundred people can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence: if officiating is beyond you, you can't ref.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantref was a medieval Welsh district, the equivalent of an English hundred, an administrative division of a county.

clue.text: Enter with force Malaysian wood

blocks.note: first meaning: to ..., push in forcefully
second meaning: a hardwood tree of Malaysia and its timber

explanation.surface: Someone forces their way into a Malaysian forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase ram in means to drive in forcibly, while ramin is a pale tropical hardwood used for mouldings.

clue.text: State of torment for one needing to reverse hair dye

indicators.note: to reverse means to go backwards, so the two letters are read from the end

blocks.note: e.g., for example, means for one
henna is a reddish dye for hair

explanation.surface: Someone in torment desperately needs to undo a bad hair-dye job.
explanation.definitionFit: Gehenna is a name for hell, the place or state of torment for the damned in Jewish and Christian scripture.

clue.text: Spineless tunneller, heading right to the back

indicators.note: the heading, the front letter, moves all the way to the rear

blocks.note: a miner digs tunnels

explanation.surface: A cowardly miner heads straight for the back of the tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spineless' looks like cowardly; in botany it means without thorns.
explanation.definitionFit: Inerm is a botanical term meaning unarmed, without thorns or spines.

clue.text: Scottish rock tune wasn’t (mostly) hard to play

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
to play with letters is to move them about freely

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Scottish rock song was not difficult to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music; it is stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Whunstane is Scots for whinstone, a hard dark basaltic stone.

clue.text: In South Australia, see clear sort of earth

indicators.note: in says the following pieces sit inside the country

blocks.note: S abbreviates south
Oz is the informal name for Australia
lo is an old word meaning see or look
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: In South Australia you can see a patch of cleared ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Australia' looks like the state; it splits into S and OZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Solonetz is a type of alkaline soil, high in sodium, found in dry regions.

clue.text: Stars unknown in the underworld

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the underworld

blocks.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Unknown stars shine in the depths of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hyades are a star cluster in the constellation Taurus, near the Pleiades.
